thread.title: Twitter: Time To Exit? - Twitter, Inc. (NYSE:TWTR)

author: Stone Fox Capital
title: Twitter: Time To Exit? - Twitter, Inc. (NYSE:TWTR)
text:
After the big run from trading in the teens as recent as last November, Twitter ( TWTR ) has now surged beyond $45. The inclusion in the S&P 500 index combined with bullish sentiment on a rebound in ad revenue might make a complete exit premature.
Image Source: Twitter presentation
Some Perspective Anybody buying Twitter around $15 in 2016 and early 2017 would clearly be prudent to cash in some of their winnings after a 200% gain. The big question though is whether to exit the whole position.
Twitter now has a market cap of nearly $35 billion. The social media company has turned into a large media asset, but the stock isn't anywhere near the $65 billion offered for a large portion of Twenty-First Century Fox ( FOX , FOXA ).
So from that perspective, Twitter is still a relatively small media company. The user base though is large and global at over 336 million MAUs. One can assume that the company has plenty of revenue upside from growing the ARPU. My previous work showed that revenues could easily reach 2.5x the Q1 levels from matching the same ARPU as Facebook ( FB ).
Even going back to Fox, the media company has over $30 billion in annual revenues showing the massive scale of the traditional media businesses and the size of the pie that Twitter is ultimately looking to attract advertiser dollars.
The stock has soared in part to the big turnaround in revenue estimates. The company has quickly gone from revenue declines to expectations that revenues will surge from $2.4 billion last year to now over $3.6 billion in 2020. The estimate is for revenues to grow roughly $400 million annually.
TWTR Revenue Estimates for Current Fiscal Year data by YCharts
Again, the expectations reversed almost on a dime after dipping nearly 8% in Q1'17. The guesstimate has to be that Twitter smokes these estimates.
The highest analyst estimate in 2019 is already up at $3.6 billion. Analysts are slow to update numbers so the stated average may not correctly reflect what the most recent updates suggest.
Twitter has seen DAUs (daily average users) surge double-digits in each of the last 6 quarters. DAUs originally topped 10% growth in Q4'16 with the below slide capturing the growth rates of the last 2 years.
Source: Twitter '18 Shareholders Meeting
One can pretty much assume that this level of growth should translate into equivalent revenue growth. The expectation though is that the social media company can start closing the ARPU gap with Facebook.
So if Twitter can grow revenues at 2x the DAU growth, the company should actually approach 25% growth. Assuming some of the trends discussed in the Q1 call does limit revenue growth this year, we'll go with the $2.9 billion revenue estimate. After that though, revenues should start rebounding towards the 25% rate or more than double the current analyst estimate at 12.5%.
Using 25%, Twitter hits revenues of $3.6 billion in 2019 and $4.5 billion in 2020. If the company is suppose to become the place to find out "What's Happening" now in the world, these revenue levels are rather small and the growth rate is meager.
As an example, Facebook expects to add $15 billion in additional revenue each of the next two years. So in 2018/2019, Facebook will add $30 billion in additional revenue and Twitter even under my bullish scenario will only add on average $800 million per year.
Twitter might appear expensive now trading at a higher forward EV/S multiple than even Snap ( SNAP ), but these numbers are based on analyst estimates that are far off base.
TWTR EV to Revenues (Forward 1y) data by YCharts
The multiple drops to an EV/S multiple of 8.9x based on my 25% growth scenario. The multiple dips even faster when using the $4.5 billion 2020 estimate.
The key though is that Twitter is now hitting the escalator up period. Note that Facebook had similar revenue levels to Twitter now when the company went public. Revenues didn't top $10 billion until around 2015 and are forecast to top $70 billion in 2019.
FB data by YCharts
Apple Example My view has long held that the Twitter versus Facebook battle was similar to Apple ( AAPL ) versus Microsoft ( MSFT ). Apple was the original leader in the computer sector before Microsoft starting crushing the market in the '90s due to some questionable tactics a la the privacy issues with Facebook now. From how the businesses were founded to the legal issues, Microsoft and Facebook have shared similarities. On the flip side, Steve Jobs and Jack Dorsey share some similarities of leaving the company they founded to starting other firms to eventually returning to turnaround their original company.
The end story with Apple and Microsoft is that Apple eventually rebounded to soar far beyond Microsoft. The lead by Microsoft was fleeting though the company maintained a revenue lead for over a decade.
AAPL Revenue (NYSE: TTM ) data by YCharts
No guarantees exist that the same scenario will occur with Twitter and Facebook. The situation though favors a run by Twitter to soon exceed the growth rates of Facebook.
The backlash with Facebook due to the privacy issues and the momentum at Twitter favors a scenario where Twitter exits 2019 with a faster growth rate. Twitter seems like an expensive stock at the moment, but the potential is enormous.
The market cap ratio as narrowed during 2018 as Twitter has soared, but the spread has grown. Facebook is now worth over $530 billion more than Twitter.
TWTR Market Cap data by YCharts
The recent rally in Twitter is only a blip in comparison to the rally at Facebook.
Takeaway The key investor takeaway is that Twitter has the ability to grow revenues far in excess of the current analyst estimates. The stock isn't as expensive when viewing the Facebook and Apple examples of the past and the ability to smash analyst estimates.
Definitely take profits on a portion of your Twitter investment, but don't rush to the exits with all of your shares. The social media company is in a position to get a whole lot bigger with an influential user base. Now isn't the time to completely exit this stock.
Disclosure: I am/we are long AAPL, TWTR.
